newsitem.title: INDIA: India's BJP to vote against Deve Gowda - deputies.
newsitem.headline: India's BJP to vote against Deve Gowda - deputies.

text.p: The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its allies decided on Friday to vote against Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in a motion of confidence, BJP legislators said.

"We have taken a decision to vote against," BJP deputy Vijay Kumar Malhotra told Reuters after a meeting between BJP leaders and its allies in the lower house of parliament, which was set to take up the motion of confidence later on Friday.
The BJP is the biggest single party in the 542-member lower house, the Lok Sabha, with 162 deputies. With its allies, it controls 193 votes.
Deve Gowda's 15-party United Front coalition has 178 deputies, while Congress, the second biggest party, controls 140, according to updated figures provided by parliament.

The BJP, which held power for 12 days last May before it resigned in the face of certain defeat in a vote of confidence, previously had not disclosed its strategy for Friday's vote, saying only that it would support neither the United Front nor Congress.

"There is no question of saving this government," BJP general secretary Venkaiah Naidu told Reuters. The Shiromani Akali Dal, which earlier this week had said it would support Deve Gowda, has decided that its eight deputies will vote with the BJP, party members said.
